title: Met32 Regulates Methionine Biosynthesis in C. albicans
summary: This cluster focuses on the regulation of methionine biosynthesis in Candida albicans, a fungus. Met32, a gene or protein, plays a central role in this process, activating Jlp12, binding to several other genes, and regulating the expression of MET genes, Sod1, and Ssu1. Met32 also interacts with Met4 and is located in the pDUP3 plasmid. C. albicans has several genes related to methionine biosynthesis, including Met6, MET15, and SOA1, and utilizes RSS. The met32 mutant strain of C. albicans is transformed into the pDUP3 plasmid. Francisella novicida, a different organism, also imports GSH, a chemical related to methionine biosynthesis.
